source_text: PAX ecce, dilectissimi fratres, Ecclesiae reddita est et, quod difficile nuper incredulis ac perfidis impossibile videbatur, ope atque ultione divina securitas nostra reparata est. In laetitiam mentes redeunt, et, tempestate pressurae ac nube discussa, tranquillitas ac serenitas refulserunt. Dandae laudes Deo, et beneficia ejus ac munera cum gratiarum actione celebranda, quamvis agere gratias nostra vox nec in persecutione cessaverit. Neque enim tantum inimico licere potest ut non, qui Dominum toto corde et anima et virtute diligimus, benedictiones ejus et laudes semper et ubique cum gloria praedicemus. Exoptatus votis omnium dies venit, et, post longae noctis horribilem tetramque caliginem, Domini luce radiatus mundus eluxit. Confessores, praeconio boni nominis claros et virtutis ac fidei laudibus gloriosos, laetis conspectibus intuemur, sanctis osculis adhaerentes, desideratos diu inexplebili cupiditate complectimur. Adest militum Christi cohors candida, qui persecutionis urgentus ferociam turbulentam stabili congressione fregerunt, parati ad patientiam carceris, armati ad tolerantiam mortis. Repugnastis fortiter saeculo, spectaculum gloriosum praebuistis Deo, secuturis fratribus fuistis exemplo. Religiosa vox Christum locuta est, in quem se semel credidisse confessa est. Illustres manus, quae non nisi divinis operibus assueverant, sacrificiis sacrilegis restiterunt. Sanctificata ora coelestibus cibis, post corpus et sanguinem Domini, profana contagia et idolorum reliquias respuerunt. Ab impio sceleratoque velamine, quo illic velabantur sacrificantium capita captiva, caput vestrum liberum mansit. Frons cum signo Dei pura, diaboli coronam ferre non potuit, coronae se Domini reservavit. Quam vos laete sinu suo excipit mater Ecclesia de praelio revertentes! quam beata, quam gaudens portas suas aperit, ut adunatis agminibus intretis, de hoste prostrato trophaea referentes! Cum triumphantibus viris et feminae veniunt, quae cum saeculo dimicantes, sexum quoque vicerunt. Veniunt et geminata militiae suae gloria virgines, et pueri annos suos virtutibus transeuntes. Necnon et caetera stantium multitudo vestram gloriam sequitur, proximis et pene conjunctis laudis insignibus vestigia vestra comitatur. Eadem et in illis sinceritas cordis, eadem fidei tenacis integritas. Inconcussis praeceptorum coelestium radicibus nixos et evangelicis traditionibus roboratos, non praescripta exilia, non destinata tormenta, non rei familiaris damna, non corporis supplicia terruerunt. Explorandae fidei praefiniebantur dies. Sed qui saeculo renuntiasse se meminit, nullum saeculi diem novit; nec tempora terrena jam computat qui aeternitatem de Deo sperat. Nemo, fratres dilectissimi, nemo hanc gloriam mutilet, nemo incorruptam stantium firmitatem maligna obtrectatione debilitet. Cum dies negantibus praestitutus excessit, quisquis professus intra diem non est, Christianum se esse confessus est. Primus est victoriae titulus, gentilium manibus apprehensum Dominum confiteri: secundus ad gloriam gradus est cauta secessione subtractum Domino reservari. Illa publica, haec privata confessio est. Ille judicem saeculi vincit, hic contentus Deo suo judice conscientiam puram cordis integritate custodit. Illic, fortitudo promptior, hic sollicitudo securior. Ille appropinquante hora sua, jam maturus inventus est; hic fortasse dilatus est qui, patrimonio derelicto, idcirco secessit quia non erat negaturus: confiteretur utique si fuisset et ipse detentus.
thought_title: Restoration of Peace to the Church
pass_a_gloss: Behold, most beloved brothers, peace has been restored to the Church, and what recently seemed impossible to the unbelieving and the faithless, our security has been repaired by divine aid and vengeance. Minds are returning to joy, and with the storm of oppression and the cloud dispersed, tranquility and serenity have shone forth. Praises must be given to God, and His benefits and gifts must be celebrated with thanksgiving, although our voice did not cease to give thanks even in persecution. For it is not possible for the enemy to be so powerful that we, who love the Lord with our whole heart and soul and strength, do not always and everywhere proclaim His blessings and praises with glory. The day longed for by all has arrived, and after the horrible and dark night, the world has shone forth radiant with the Lord's light. We gaze upon the confessors with joyful countenances, clinging to them with holy kisses, embracing those we have longed for with insatiable desire. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers is present, who broke the fierce fury of persecution with a stable confrontation, prepared for the patience of prison, armed for the tolerance of death. You have strongly resisted the world, you have presented a glorious spectacle to God, you have been an example to your brothers who will follow. The religious voice has spoken of Christ, in whom it has confessed to have once believed. Illustrious hands, which were accustomed only to divine works, have resisted sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by celestial foods, after the body and blood of the Lord, have rejected profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your head, freed from the impious and wicked veil with which the heads of those sacrificing were captive, has remained free. Your forehead, marked with the sign of God, could not bear the crown of the devil, but has reserved itself for the crown of the Lord. How joyfully the mother Church receives you, returning from battle, in her bosom! How blessed, how joyful she opens her gates, that you may enter with assembled troops, bringing back trophies from the defeated enemy! With the triumphant men, women also come, who, fighting with the world, have also conquered their sex. The virgins also come, with double glory of their military service, and children who have surpassed their years with virtues. The multitude of the rest of those standing also follows your glory, accompanying your footsteps with the insignia of praise closely joined. The same sincerity of heart and the same tenacity of faith are in them. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by evangelical traditions, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, nor by destined torments, nor by losses of family, nor by bodily punishments. Days were being sought to test their faith. But whoever remembers that they have renounced the world knows no day of the world; nor does he who hopes for eternity from God now calculate earthly times. No one, most beloved brothers, no one should mutilate this glory, no one should weaken the incorrupt firmness of those standing with malignant detraction. When the day appointed for those who deny has passed, whoever has not professed within the day has confessed to being a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord, apprehended by the hands of the Gentiles; the second step to glory is to be reserved for the Lord by cautious secession. The former is public, the latter is private confession. The former conquers the judge of the world, the latter, content with his own judge, God, keeps a pure conscience with the integrity of heart. In the former, fortitude is more prompt, in the latter, solicitude is more secure. The former, with his hour approaching, has already been found mature; the latter, perhaps delayed, who, having abandoned his patrimony, withdrew for the same reason that he would not deny: he would certainly have confessed if he had also been detained.

pass_b_english: Behold, most beloved brothers, peace has been restored to the Church, and what once seemed impossible to the unbelieving and the faithless — our security — has been repaired by divine aid and vengeance; minds are turning back to joy, the storm of oppression and the cloud have been dispersed, and tranquility and serenity now shine forth. Praises must be given to God, and His benefits and gifts celebrated with thanksgiving, for our voice never ceased giving thanks even in the midst of persecution. Indeed, the enemy cannot be so powerful that we, who love the Lord with our whole heart, soul, and strength, would fail to proclaim His blessings and praises always and everywhere with glory.

The day longed for by all has arrived, and after the horrible, dark night the world has shone radiant with the Lord's light. We gaze upon the confessors with joyful faces, clinging to them with holy kisses and embracing those we have yearned for with an insatiable desire. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers stands before us, having broken the fierce fury of persecution through a steadfast confrontation, prepared for the patience of prison and armed for the tolerance of death. You have resisted the world mightily, offered a glorious spectacle to God, and become an example for the brothers who will follow.

The religious voice has spoken of Christ, confessing that it once believed in Him. Illustrious hands, accustomed only to divine works, have refused sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by the heavenly food of the Lord's body and blood have rejected profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your head, freed from the impious and wicked veil that covered the heads of those who sacrificed, remains free; your forehead, marked with the sign of God, could not bear the devil's crown but has reserved itself for the Lord's crown. How joyfully the mother Church receives you, returning from battle, into her bosom! How blessed and joyful she opens her gates so that you may enter with assembled troops, bearing trophies from the defeated enemy! With the triumphant men come women who, fighting the world, have also conquered their own sex; virgins arrive with a double glory of their warfare, and children surpass their years through virtue. The multitude of the rest who stand follows your glory, tracing your footsteps with insignia of praise closely joined. The same sincerity of heart and the same tenacity of faith dwell in them. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by evangelical traditions, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, destined torments, loss of family, or bodily punishments. Days were appointed to test their faith, yet whoever remembers that he has renounced the world knows no day of the world, and he who hopes for eternity from God no longer calculates earthly times.

No one, most beloved brothers, should mutilate this glory, nor should anyone weaken the incorrupt firmness of those who stand with malignant detraction. When the day appointed for those who deny has passed, whoever has not professed within that day has confessed to being a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord, seized by the hands of the Gentiles; the second step toward glory is to be reserved for the Lord by a cautious withdrawal. The former is a public confession, the latter a private one. The public confession conquers the judge of the world, while the private confession, content with God as its judge, preserves a pure conscience through integrity of heart. In the public confession fortitude is more prompt; in the private confession solicitude is more secure. The public confessor, with his hour approaching, has already been found mature; the private confessor, perhaps delayed, who abandoned his patrimony and withdrew because he would not deny, would certainly have confessed if he had also been detained.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text, including the distinction between public and private confession (Ille... hic...) and the conditional nature of the final clause (si fuisset). Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source.
